Triumph Reveals the 2027 Tiger 1200 as the Most Everything Adventure Bike It Ever Made
47 photos
Photo: Triumph
The last time British bike maker Triumph seriously upgraded the Tiger 1200 adventure motorcycle was some two years ago, at the beginning of 2024. The changes made back then are fresh enough to still be relevant, but, for one reason or another, the company decided to update the bike again – making it in the process the most accessible, most advanced and most versatile large-capacity bike of this kind ever made by Triumph.
Triumph's changes target everything, from the mechanical bits that influence the performance numbers to the way the bike behaves and handles on the road, with all these upgrades topped off by a visual refresh.
I'll start, as usual, with the bike's frame, which remains the same tubular steel frame configuration as before, fitted with aluminum outriggers, a subframe, and a swingarm made of the same material.
The suspension system that ties into the frame is described by Triumph as the most sophisticated semi-active setup the company has ever used on any of its products. Responsible for that bold description is the Showa Eera Heightflex self-lowering suspension system.
Born into the world some eight years ago, the tech comes with three damping settings, and, on top of that, it can automatically lower the seat by 30 mm when the bike stops, and can make life easier for riders when the bike needs to be fitted on a center stand.
Photo: Triumph The suspension system, which consists of 49 mm forks and a monoshock, supports wheels sized 19 inches at the front and 17 inches at the rear, which move under the power supplied by the mighty 1200 triple engine (1,160cc) and the six-speed transmission that controls it.
The powerplant has been at the receiving end of some serious upgrades that targeted the cylinder heads, pistons, inlet and exhaust valves (the larger exhaust tech is a stainless steel 3-into-1 header system), and fuel injection. The changes made to these parts led to the engine now developing eight horsepower more than before, for a total of 156 hp at 9,250 rpm.
Torque levels for the new Tiger 1200 stand at 130 Nm at 6,750 rpm, and there are up to eight ride modes the bike can be set in: Road, Rain, Eco, Sport, Off-road, Off-road Pro, and two configurable ones.
The new Tiger 1200 brings along, as another novelty, front and rear Bosch radar, which works in conjunction with cornering ABS, traction control, and the six-axis IMU (Inertial Measurement Unit).
Photo: Triumph The revised and improved engine goes hand in hand with updates the Brits performed to the way the bike interacts and connects to the rider. More specifically, Triumph went for a new seven-inch touchscreen that runs wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto, something not many motorcycles out there are capable of. There is new switchgear on deck, alongside a cooled phone compartment with USB-C charging,
Without affecting the bike's original dimensions and overall stance, Triumph also revised the bodywork of the new Tiger, changing the lines and appearance of the fuel tank, radiator cowls, beak and windscreen. There is a new LED headlight up front, complete with cornering functionality.
Triumph plans to offer the 2027 Tiger 1200 in four different versions, namely GT Pro, Rally Pro, GT Explorer and Rally Explorer. Setting them apart are, among other things, the size of the fuel tank, the choice of wheels, various protective components, and the riding position.
There are also different colors to be had depending on the model. Triumph already lists the five new two-wheelers on its configurators, complete with pricing information. Important to note is the fact that, despite the many changes that made it into the design, the price for the new versions is not significantly higher than the 2024 incarnations.
Photo: Triumph You can read all about pricing and available colors in the lines below, but before you do that, I should also mention the new rides will be available at dealers from December 2026.
2027 Triumph Tiger 1200 GT Pro (Sapphire Black, Aluminum Silver/Pacific Blue) - $22,995 2027 Triumph Tiger 1200 Rally Pro (Matt Khaki Green, Ash Grey) - $24,445 2027 Triumph Tiger 1200 GT Explorer (Aluminum Silver/Pacific Blue, Granite) - $24,995 2027 Triumph Tiger 1200 Rally Explorer (Ash Grey/Sapphire Black, Matt Khaki Green) - $26,445
Triumph presented the new Tiger 1200 a few days before the largest motorcycle show in the world, the Esposizione Internazionale Ciclo Motociclo e Accessori (EICMA), opens its doors in Milan, Italy, next week. The bike maker will attend the event, and it will probably bring this new bike along.
autoevolution will be on location at the Fiera Milano Rho to bring you all the hottest bikes and moto technologies to be presented there, including the ones made by Triumph. As a reminder, EICMA opens on November 5, but you should expect many of the premieres to be presented before that, so stay tuned for more in the coming days.
